I have been farming here in Quzhou for five years now, and I have learned that the wheat-maize rotation is the only sensible way to use my 12 mu of land on the North China Plain. My household has five people, but some of them work off-farm, so I cannot manage too much labor myself. That is why I stick with what I know: winter wheat followed by summer maize.

For wheat this winter, I will plant the full 12 mu with an improved variety called Luyuan 502. I buy fresh seed every year from the market because my own saved seed does not grow as well. Before planting, I will use rotary tillage to break up the soil and make a smooth seedbed. For fertilizer, I will put down compound fertilizer as a basal dose and then topdress with urea. In total, I expect to apply about 15 to 16 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. Wheat needs water, so I will irrigate four times from the well—before winter, at green-up, at jointing, and during grain filling. I also need to spray pesticides about six times in total for weeds, insects, and the rust diseases that sometimes come. If the weather cooperates, I should get around 575 kg per mu.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize on the same 12 mu. Time is short, so I will use no-tillage planting to save labor and get the crop in quickly. I will use a hybrid variety, Denghai 605, because hybrids give much better yields. For maize, I will apply less fertilizer than wheat—about 11 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu—since maize here does not need as much. I will irrigate twice, usually at the jointing stage and during silking, depending on rainfall. Pesticides are needed for armyworms and weeds, so I plan to spray about eight times total. I expect the maize to yield around 616 kg per mu.

My reasoning is simple: this rotation has worked for me these past five years, the well gives me reliable water, and with limited labor at home, no-tillage maize after rotary-tilled wheat is the most practical system I can manage.
